sql.title: Quick lab: use one query as an input
sql.prompt: Find cities of companies making products bought by Joe Blow.
steps: Predict the output columns and row count.
Copy and run the query with the lecture data.
Show the result and explain any difference from your prediction.

code.label: Query from slide 68
code.text:
SELECT c.city
FROM Company AS c
WHERE c.name IN (
  SELECT pr.maker
  FROM Purchase AS p
  JOIN Product AS pr ON p.product = pr.name
  WHERE p.buyer = 'Joe Blow'
);

demos:
The inner query returns maker names.
The outer query converts qualifying makers into company cities.

sql.title: Quick lab: test whether a matching row exists

FROM Product AS p1
WHERE p1.maker = 'Gizmo-Works'

    SELECT 1
    FROM Product AS p2
    WHERE p2.maker <> 'Gizmo-Works'
      AND p2.name = p1.name
  );

demos: The outer product is returned when the correlated subquery finds at least one competitor row with the same name.

sql.title: Quick lab: express a set difference
sql.prompt: Return R pairs that have no matching pair in S.
steps: Predict the output columns and row count.
Copy and run the query with the lecture data.
Show the result and explain any difference from your prediction.

code.label: Query from slide 73
code.text:
SELECT R.A, R.B
FROM R
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1
  FROM S
  WHERE S.A = R.A AND S.B = R.B
);

demos:
Each R row is kept only when no equal (A,B) row exists in S.
This is a NULL-safer anti-match pattern.
